name: Fusarium Wilt of Plantain
scientificName: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (subtropical race)
description: A vascular wilt disease of plantain caused by Fusarium oxysporum. It affects the plant's water-conducting tissue, causing wilting and eventual death. Subtropical race is less aggressive than TR4 but still economically damaging.
symptoms: Yellowing of older leaves starting from margins
Leaf petioles splitting at the base
Progressive wilting from older to younger leaves
causes: Soil-borne pathogen entering through root tips
Waterlogged or compacted soils stressing plants
Spread through contaminated tools and irrigation water
treatments: Remove infected plants and apply lime to affected area
prevention: Improve soil drainage and avoid waterlogging
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Quarantine affected fields and restrict movement of soil
